issue: Does Honeycutt v. United States bar joint and several liability for forfeiture under 18 U.S.C. § 981(a)(1)(C), given that § 981(a)(1)(C) lacks § 853(a)'s 'the person obtained' language?

sides.position: Honeycutt does not apply to forfeiture under § 981(a)(1)(C), so joint and several forfeiture liability remains permissible because the 'the person obtained' language that drove Honeycutt is absent from that statute.
cases: United States v. Sexton, 894 F.3d 787, 799 (6th Cir. 2018)
United States v. Peithman, 917 F.3d 635, 652 (8th Cir. 2019)

sides.position: Honeycutt applies to forfeiture under § 981(a)(1)(C), so a court may no longer impose joint and several liability for proceeds a co-conspirator obtained.
cases: United States v. Gjeli, 867 F.3d 418, 427 n.16, 428 (3d Cir. 2017)

quote: We note that a circuit split has developed over whether Honeycutt applies to a forfeiture under 18 U.S.C. § 981(a)(1)(C).
cite: United States v. Channon (Brandi), 973 F.3d 1105 (10th Cir. 2020)
